deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a personal, non-mathematical note in Hilbert's notebook (bundle 600:3, fol. 139). It has two parts.

(1) A heading 'Empfehlenswerte Bücher:' ('Recommended books:') with a single entry. The image reads 'Weissmann: Descendenztheorie' (written 'Dessendenztheorie'), not 'Vererbungstheorie'. This almost certainly refers to August Weismann, 'Vorlesungen über Descendenztheorie' (Jena, 1902). The entry was therefore written in or after 1902.

(2) A dated list of numbers running from 1883 to 1897. The pairs are: 180 (10.2.83), 179 (20.5.85), 180 (22.7.87), 181 (27.7.87), 180,5 (4.11.88), 190 (19.12.88, 'mit br.[?] Umschlag'), 90 (5.4.91), 90 (4.7.91, 'm. Beil.'), 90,5 (19.7.91, ditto), 190 (6.7.92, 'mit Umschlag'), 192 (9.11.93, ditto), 90,8 (4.5.95), 190,9 (20.6.96), 90,5 (18.7.96), 92 (14.8.96), 193 (5.9.96), 92,1 (17.7.97), 92,1 (1.10.97; written '921', probably with the comma omitted).

The most plausible reading (my interpretation, not stated on the page) is a record of body weight. Before 1891 the values would be in German Pfund (500 g), around 180 Pfund = 90 kg. From 1891 on they appear to be in kg, around 90 to 92 kg. Some entries over 190 carry the note 'mit Umschlag' or 'm. Beil.'. Whether those are heavier because something extra was worn or carried, or because they revert to Pfund, cannot be decided from the page alone.

The list runs from Hilbert's student years in Königsberg (age 21) to his early Göttingen years. No derivation, problem or computation is present.
errors: No mathematical content, so no mathematical errors.
